subject: Forecasting playbook refresh + scenario lab sign-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sales Team <sales@redwood.com>; ben.carter@redwood.com; lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 25 Jan 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Forecasting playbook refresh + scenario lab sign-up

Team —

Quick heads-up: Finance and RevOps pushed an update to the forecast category definitions (Commit / Best Case / Pipeline) after the audit last quarter. The changes are focused on clarifying qualification gates and documentation required to move deals into Commit. Highlights: 

- Commit now requires a signed commercial term sheet or an explicit, recorded verbal agreement on both price and timing.
- Best Case remains as deals with active technical alignment and verbal buying signals but missing commercial terms.
- Pipeline: opportunities we intend to pursue but with open qualification gaps.

I attached the one-page summary (forecast_definition_v2.pdf) and a short slide deck we'll use in two 45-minute scenario labs next week (scenario_lab_slides.pptx). Please: 

1) Read the one-pager before your regional standups this week.
2) Update any deals that you think should move categories by EOD Wednesday. If you’re unsure, add the deal to the shared sign-up sheet for a 10‑minute 1:1 review during the scenario labs.
3) Encourage AEs to include the required doc references in the HubSpot record (pricing email, signed term sheet link, or procurement ticket).

We want consistent commit hygiene heading into mid‑quarter review; small principle: if you cannot point to the commercial commitment, it’s not Commit.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: forecast_definition_v2.pdf (one-page), scenario_lab_slides.pptx (15 slides)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sales Team <sales@redwood.com>; karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 26 Jan 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Forecasting playbook refresh + scenario lab sign-up

Marissa —

Thanks for the note and materials. Quick question on edge cases: we have a deal (ACME-2345) where the customer has approved PO language internally and the AE has a thread from their procurement lead saying they expect to release a PO in 7–10 business days, but no signed term sheet yet. AE has committed to a go‑live date contingent on PO arrival. Under the new definition, does that count as Commit or Best Case?

I want to make the right call before I update the board.

—Ben

Ben / Jillian —

Thanks for the quick responses. Short answer for ACME-2345: classify as Best Case until we have either (a) a signed term sheet or (b) a procurement ticket with explicit approval + copy of the PO or confirmation from procurement that a PO is issued (a screenshot of the procurement system OK). The procurement email alone that says "we expect to issue a PO" is insufficient for Commit under the new policy.

Operational notes: 
- If an AE can produce the procurement ticket number and a screenshot or email from the procurement approver that indicates the PO has been issued, that meets the Commit requirement. 
- For deals stuck between Best Case and Commit, add them to the scenario lab sign-up so we can walk the specific artifacts together — I’ll run a 45‑minute session on Monday and Wednesday next week. Sign-up: signup-sheet.csv (please add owner, deal id, 10‑minute slot).

I'll update the playbook doc with this example and post it to the Playbook link (https://redwood-infra.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/finance/ForecastingPlaybookV2). For any immediate escalations before the lab, ping me or Karthik directly.

Appreciate everyone's help tightening pre‑quarter numbers.

—Marissa
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
